title: 009 — GitHub: Actions workflow lockfiles, AI Scan and agentic autofix
html:
009 — GitHub: Actions workflow lockfiles, AI Scan and agentic autofix

The one idea: In mid-October 2026, GitHub shipped three supply-chain and code-security features. Workflow lockfiles (preview) pin every action your workflow runs to a reviewed commit, so a moved tag can't sneak in new code. AI Scan (GA) finds vulnerabilities in languages CodeQL doesn't cover, including Blazor, Terraform and Dockerfiles. Agentic autofix (GA) lets Copilot fix code scanning alerts and open a draft PR.

Added 2026-10-17 · Announced 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15 by GitHub

1. What it is

Feature Status What it does
Workflow dependency lockfiles Public preview (Free, Team, Enterprise Cloud) .github/workflows/actions.lock records the exact commit of every action, transitive action and reusable workflow a workflow uses
Require lockfile policy Public preview Admins at enterprise, org or repo level can require lockfiles for workflows
AI Scan for pull requests GA AI-based vulnerability findings on PR changes, next to CodeQL results, for PHP, Shell, Terraform (HCL), Dockerfiles, JSP and Blazor
Agentic autofix for code scanning GA (Enterprise Cloud) Assign an alert to Copilot. It edits the code, reruns CodeQL to confirm the alert is closed, and opens a draft PR

2. Why it matters

  • Tags are mutable. uses: some/action@v3 can point at different code tomorrow. Real supply-chain attacks have moved tags on popular actions to steal CI secrets. A lockfile closes that gap without hand-pinning SHAs everywhere.
  • Blazor and infrastructure code get scanned. CodeQL doesn't cover Blazor components, Terraform or Dockerfiles. AI Scan fills that gap for a .NET and Azure stack.
  • The security backlog shrinks. Old alerts on the default branch can be handed to Copilot in batches of up to 25 per PR. Fixes are checked by rerunning CodeQL before anyone reviews them.

3. How it works

---
title: Workflow lockfile — what a run executes
---
flowchart LR
    W["Workflow uses some/action@v3"] --> L["actions.lock<br/>v3 = commit abc123"]
    L --> R["Runner executes commit abc123"]
    T["Tag v3 moved to commit def456"] -.->|"ignored until lockfile updated"| R
    D["Dependabot PR"] -->|"bumps version and lockfile together"| L

Once a workflow is onboarded, every dependency must have a lockfile entry, and Actions runs the recorded commits even if a tag or branch moves. Dependabot updates the workflow and the lockfile entry in the same PR. A CI step can check that the lockfile isn't stale without changing files.

4. How to use it

Lockfiles:

  1. Install the GitHub CLI extension from the github/gh-actions-lock repository (gh actions-lock).
  2. Generate the lockfile for one workflow at a time, review the commits it records, and commit .github/workflows/actions.lock with the workflow.
  3. Add a staleness check to CI, then turn on the Require lockfile policy when all workflows are onboarded.

AI Scan: turn on code scanning and the repository's AI Scan setting. Findings show on the PR's Conversation and Files changed tabs with an "AI" label, often with a suggested fix. Public repos get it free. Private and internal repos need GitHub Code Security or Advanced Security. No Copilot licence is needed.

Agentic autofix:

  1. An enterprise admin enables the "Agentic autofix" policy. An org or repo admin then turns it on in Code Security settings.
  2. Click Assign to Copilot on an alert, or select up to 25 alerts in the list.
  3. From automation, call the "Update a code scanning alert" REST API with assignees: ["copilot-swe-agent[bot]"].
  4. Review the draft PR. Comment on it to ask for changes.

In practice: start lockfiles on the workflows that hold deployment secrets (Azure login, NuGet publish) first. They are the most valuable targets.

5. Trade-offs and limits

  • A lockfile doesn't vet code. It only freezes what you reviewed. Review an action before you lock it.
  • Lockfiles are in preview. The file format and commands may change.
  • AI Scan is advisory. Its findings can't fail the code scanning check or block a merge through rulesets. It doesn't run on fork PRs or Dependabot PRs.
  • Autofix costs credits. It uses Code Security AI credits plus Actions minutes, needs a Copilot billing method, and works only on default-branch alerts. It reruns CodeQL, not your test suite, so CI on the draft PR still matters.
  • Adopt now or wait? Turn on AI Scan now where you have the licence, since it costs nothing to review. Pilot lockfiles on one repo. Use agentic autofix for low-risk alert classes first.

6. Where it fits

  • GitHub Actions: workflows, reusable workflows and pinning.
  • CI/CD fundamentals: supply-chain controls in a pipeline.
  • Security engineering: static analysis and the vulnerability lifecycle.
  • GitHub Copilot code review via API: the earlier Copilot automation note.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why is uses: owner/action@v3 a supply-chain risk, and how does a lockfile differ from pinning a SHA in the workflow file?
  2. What keeps the lockfile current when an action releases a new version?
  3. Which parts of a .NET and Azure repo does AI Scan cover that CodeQL doesn't?
  4. Why can't AI Scan findings block a merge today, and what would you use for blocking checks instead?
  5. How does agentic autofix check its own fix, and what does it not check?

Sources

  • GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles in public preview — GitHub Changelog, 14 Oct 2026
  • AI Scan for pull requests generally available — GitHub Changelog, 15 Oct 2026
  • Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts general availability — GitHub Changelog, 15 Oct 2026
